title: Flexible Constraint Validation
description: You are given a string formula containing only three types of characters: '(', ')', and '*'. The character '*' can act as a left parenthesis '(', a right parenthesis ')', or as an empty string "". A string is considered valid under the following conditions: any left parenthesis must have a corresponding right parenthesis, every right parenthesis must have a corresponding left parenthesis, and '*' can be flexibly resolved to satisfy these pairing rules. Determine if the formula is valid.

examples.explanation: The '*' can be treated as an empty string, making it "()" which is balanced.
The '*' can be treated as '(' to balance the two trailing ')' characters, yielding "(())".
